items.title: Shocking secret you won’t believe! Emotional arousal in clickbait headlines

judge.evidence_topic: The purpose of this paper is to fill a gap in the literature by providing empirical evidence of how clickbait headlines affect online users’ emotional and behavioral responses, specifically emotional arousal and intention to read news.
judge.evidence_empirical: An experiment was conducted primarily to examine the levels of emotional arousal evoked by two treatment groups of online news headlines, news and clickbait, compared to a neutral control group.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (experimento) publicado em 2019 que investiga os efeitos de manchetes clickbait na excitação emocional e intenção de leitura dos usuários, sem recorte político. Os dados extraídos estão corretos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Effects of Clickbait Headlines on User Responses: An Empirical Investigation

judge.evidence_topic: This study investigates the influence of a conventional method of delivering news headlines, clickbait, on online users’ perceptions and responses.
judge.evidence_empirical: An experiment was conducted on two groups of news headlines—traditional news and clickbait— to provide empirical evidence of the effects of clickbait on online users.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (experimento) sobre os efeitos de manchetes clickbait em usuários, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão. O método descrito no resumo condiz com o extraído, e o achado principal é sustentado pelo texto do resumo.

items.title: Clickbait—Trust and Credibility of Digital News

judge.evidence_topic: To understand their impact on the credibility of news items, we designed and conducted an experiment on news articles from the Web is-Clickbait-17 dataset.
judge.evidence_empirical: 200 participants (100 each of English-speaking American and English-speaking Indian) were instructed to click and read through any two articles of their choice and fill a credibility questionnaire.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (experimento) que investiga o impacto de manchetes clickbait na credibilidade percebida pelos leitores, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão. O método e o achado principal estão corretamente descritos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Aggregation, Clickbait and Their Effect on Perceptions of Journalistic Credibility and Quality

judge.evidence_topic: This study uses published original and aggregated news articles as stimuli in two online experiments to test readers’ perceptions of news aggregation and clickbait.
judge.evidence_empirical: This study uses published original and aggregated news articles as stimuli in two online experiments to test readers’ perceptions of news aggregation and clickbait.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (experimentos) que investiga o efeito de manchetes clickbait na percepção dos leitores, alinhando-se ao pedido. O método e o achado principal estão corretamente descritos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: The curiosity effect: Information seeking in the contemporary news environment

judge.evidence_topic: In two studies (a lab experiment and a field test), we examine how the presentation of news information—traditional, summary news headlines or clickbait, curiosity news headlines—influences the attitudinal and behavioral components of news seeking.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two studies (a lab experiment and a field test), we examine how the presentation of news information—traditional, summary news headlines or clickbait, curiosity news headlines—influences the attitudinal and behavioral components of news seeking.
judge.reason: O artigo é empírico, trata do efeito de manchetes de curiosidade (clickbait) no comportamento de busca de notícias e os achados são sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Attention Grabbing through Forward Reference: An ERP Study on Clickbait and Top News Stories

items.title: AI vs. Human-Authored Headlines: Evaluating the Effectiveness, Trust, and Linguistic Features of ChatGPT-Generated Clickbait and Informative Headlines in Digital News

judge.evidence_topic: This research assesses readers’ reactions to different headline styles as tested on a sample of 624 students from Timisoara, Romania... Clickbait headlines, regardless of their source, were considered misleading and rated as manipulative (44.7%). In addition, 54.5% of respondents reported a decrease in trust regarding publications that frequently use clickbait techniques.
judge.evidence_empirical: This research assesses readers’ reactions to different headline styles as tested on a sample of 624 students from Timisoara, Romania
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico que analisa a reação de leitores a manchetes clickbait, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão. Os achados extraídos estão diretamente sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Are ChatGPT-Generated Headlines Better Attention Grabbers than Human-Authored Ones? An Assessment of Salient Features Driving Engagement with Online Media

judge.evidence_topic: To assess the reaction of online readers to headlines (clickbait or click-worthy), an online survey was applied...
